same tools serve any desk, each in its own `memory/` corner.

declarations.documentation:
The memory INDEX read from the CURRENT workspace — the one record mapping each saved key to its
one-line summary (empty when nothing is saved). Callers must already stand inside the memory scope:
`index` wraps this for ordinary reads, and a mutation's critical section calls it after its own
scope install (the task's first move), so the read and the write resolve the same key. Read TOTAL
(`json.entries`), so a missing or malformed value degrades to the empty record rather than throwing
into an every-turn injection.
declarations.name: stored_index

declarations.documentation:
How many code points of a summary one index line carries. This is the ONE cap the every-turn
injection has, and the asymmetry is deliberate: the number of LINES stays uncapped, because a line that
is not shown is a memory the model does not know exists — and it will not search for what it does not
suspect, so no marker could repair the omission. Bounding each line hides no memory, which is exactly
what makes it safe where a count cap is not. 120 points is a line of prose, and deliberately less than
`search_excerpt_limit`: a summary can never cost more than the excerpt that would show the note's own
words.
declarations.name: index_summary_limit

declarations.documentation:
One index line's summary text: rendered, folded to a single line, and cut to `index_summary_limit`
with an explicit marker — never silently, on the same discipline as `search`'s caps. The cut is DISPLAY
only: the stored summary is untouched, and the note itself is what `recall` answers with. A rolling note
appended to nightly is where this bites — its summary is the one that grows without anyone ever deciding
to grow it.
declarations.name: bounded_summary

declarations.checkedType: agent(...record) -> array[string] with delete | get | list | set

declarations.name: index_lines

declarations.checkedType: agent(body: string, key: string, summary: string) -> string with exclusive
declarations.documentation:
Tool: save a note to your persistent memory under a short key (e.g. "user/name",
"prefs/timezone"). You give a one-line @summary@ (shown back to you every turn in the memory index)
and the full @body@ (read on demand with recall). Both survive restarts, so save durable facts,
preferences and decisions — not this turn's scratch work. Re-using a key overwrites it. ALWAYS write a
real summary — but an IDENTIFIER, not an abstract: it is what you see every turn, and the note itself
stays reachable (recall reads it by key, search finds it by its contents), so do not pack the body into
the summary. A summary running past one line is cut in the index anyway.
declarations.name: remember

parameters.documentation: A one-line summary, shown every turn in the index.
parameters.label: summary

parameters.documentation: The full note, read back with recall.
parameters.label: body

body.description: The full note, read back with recall.

summary.description: A one-line summary, shown every turn in the index.

declarations.documentation:
How many matching memories one `search` answers with. The bound is the point of searching rather
than injecting: a result that dumps more than the every-turn index would defeat its own purpose, and a
recall question that needs more than a handful of candidates needs a better pattern, which the cut
marker asks for.
declarations.name: search_match_limit

declarations.documentation:
How many code points of a body one match's excerpt carries — two or three sentences, enough to judge
whether this is the note being looked for. Reading a note in FULL stays `recall`'s job, so the excerpt
is a pointer, never a replacement.
declarations.name: search_excerpt_limit

declarations.documentation:
How many code points of the excerpt window sit BEFORE the occurrence, so a match arrives with the run
up to it rather than flush against the window's edge.
declarations.name: search_excerpt_lead

declarations.documentation:
Whether @pattern@ occurs in @value@ ignoring case — the ONE match test behind `search`, applied
alike to a key, a summary and a body. Case is folded on both sides because stored prose capitalizes at
its own discretion ("Docker", "docker") while a model recalling it types whatever it remembers, and
a case-sensitive miss would read to the caller as 'not stored'.
declarations.name: folded_contains
declarations.signature: agent folded_contains(value: string, pattern: string) -> boolean

declarations.documentation:
The memory key of the entry named @name@ sitting directly under the entries subdirectory @parent@ —
the separator appears only where there is a parent, so a top-level key stays bare (`"notes"`, never
`"/notes"`).
declarations.name: descended_key
declarations.signature: agent descended_key(parent: string, name: string) -> string

declarations.documentation:
Every stored memory key, read from the LISTING — callers must already stand inside the entries scope
(`memory/entries`), and the keys come back relative to it, exactly as the model spells them. A key is
path-like ("user/name"), so `store.list` answers a `branch` for every group and the walk has to
descend; it descends BREADTH-FIRST through an explicit worklist rather than by self-recursion, because
recursion here is a real delegation per group and parks a durable frame chain — a read-only tool must
leave nothing behind.
declarations.name: entry_keys

declarations.documentation:

declarations.documentation:
The window of @body@ around the FIRST occurrence of @pattern@ — one line, `search_excerpt_limit`
code points wide, with `search_excerpt_lead` of them ahead of the match. A body that matched on its key
or summary alone has no occurrence to centre on, so the window falls back to the note's opening; either
way the excerpt says outright where it was cut, because a model handed a silently clipped note answers
as if it had read the whole thing.

declarations.checkedType: agent(pattern: string) -> string with delete | get | list | set
declarations.documentation:
Tool: SEARCH your persistent memory for a pattern — the way to find a note you remember the CONTENT
of but not the key. @pattern@ is plain text, not a regular expression and not a query language: it
matches wherever it occurs as a substring, and case is ignored ("docker" finds "Docker"). Unlike the
'[memory index]' block you are shown each turn, this reads the FULL BODY of every saved note, so it
finds what a one-line summary left out. Each match comes back as its `- key: summary` line plus a short
excerpt of the note around the match; a cut excerpt and any matches beyond the ones shown are always
stated outright, so read a note in full with recall(key) and narrow the pattern when told there is more.
Matches arrive in stored key order (shallow keys first), NOT by relevance — nothing here ranks, so when
there are more than you were shown, narrow the pattern rather than trust the first ones to be the best.
Nothing is written — searching never changes a memory.
declarations.name: search

parameters.documentation: Plain text to look for, matched as a substring anywhere in a key, a summary or a note body; case is ignored.
